rows.title: Do RESTful API design rules have an impact on the understandability of Web APIs?
rows.authors: Justus Bogner; Sebastian Kotstein; Timo Pfaff
rows.abstract: Abstract Context Web APIs are one of the most used ways to expose application functionality on the Web, and their understandability is important for efficiently using the provided resources. rows.abstract: Background: Data quality is vital in software analytics, particularly for machine learning (ML) applications like software defect prediction (SDP). rows.authors: Justus Bogner; Sebastian Kotstein; Daniel Abajirov; Timothy Ernst

rows.abstract: According to ISO/IEC 9126-1, usability refers to a software's capability for being understood, learned, used, and attractive to the user under specific conditions. rows.abstract: Usability refers to a software's capability for being understood, learned, used, and attractive to the user under specific conditions. The main goal of this paper is to develop a set of usability heuristics and guidelines for designing RESTful APIs. This is done through a comprehensive analysis of REST principles using an extended, general-purpose usability model as a guide. The efficacy of these heuristics and guidelines is tested with a case study, namely, the REST API for Twitter developers.

rows.title: FindICI: Using machine learning to detect linguistic inconsistencies between code and natural language descriptions in infrastructure-as-code
rows.authors: Nemania Borovits; Indika Kumara; Dario Di Nucci; Parvathy Krishnan
rows.abstract: Linguistic anti-patterns are recurring poor practices concerning inconsistencies in the naming, documentation, and implementation of an entity.
